Every exit code below was read from the process's own status immediately after the command, never from the tail of a pipeline. NO `terraform apply` WAS RUN and none appears in any transcript. plan_repro.sh's refusal allowlist and its stage-2 empty-state equivalence check were not weakened; a stage-0 truncated-checkout refusal and exit code 11 were ADDED, and both of its branches are demonstrated firing below.

the_detector_comparison_that_is_the_whol.reading: `git ls-files --deleted` — the obvious question — answers ZERO on a tree that is missing files, because the aborted checkout never wrote the index and `--deleted` compares the working tree against it. `git status --short` answers 7,613 while 7,575 of 7,577 files were present, so it over-reports by three thousand: it is a detector, not a census. And the four prefix counts are all zero, which is why `terraform validate` is green here. THREE DIFFERENT WRONG ANSWERS TO ONE QUESTION.
the_detector_comparison_that_is_the_whol.note_on_severity_varying: Revision 1 of this file measured the same hazard at a 136-character parent and recorded 6,417 of 7,548 paths missing. At 125 characters against `7535670` only 2 of 7,577 are missing. THE SEVERITY IS NOT STABLE AND MUST NOT BE THE SIGNAL. Both runs share the load-bearing property — zero missing under all four Terraform-relevant prefixes — and that is what the guard is written against.

the_fix_added_to_plan_repro_sh.what: A new STAGE 0 that runs before Terraform, before the AWS CLI and before any file is written. It takes the census from `git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only` — the one list a failed checkout cannot corrupt, because the object transfer succeeded — sorts it, diffs it against a `find` over the working tree, and refuses with a NEW exit code 11 naming the missing paths, their per-top-directory breakdown, and the four prefix counts.
the_fix_added_to_plan_repro_sh.what_it_is_not: It does not touch the `tf` allowlist, the `-destroy`/`-refresh-only`/`-auto-approve` refusals, the stage-2 empty-state equivalence check, or the stage-2b build-input check. It ADDS a refusal; it relaxes nothing.
the_fix_added_to_plan_repro_sh.second_refusal_in_the_same_stage: `index entries == 0 && HEAD paths > 0` is refused on its own, because that is the signature of the aborted checkout and it is what makes every index-relative answer unreliable.
the_fix_added_to_plan_repro_sh.the_prune_list_is_measured_not_asserted: The filesystem walk skips `.git` plus `node_modules .venv __pycache__ .terraform out dist`, and each of those six is FIRST checked against this HEAD's own path list; a name that HEAD uses is dropped from the prune list and walked. Measured at `7535670`: 0 tracked paths contain any of the six as a path segment, 0 case-collisions that would false-positive on a case-insensitive filesystem, 0 symlinks.
the_fix_added_to_plan_repro_sh.cost: 0.57 s for the set difference against a 7,577-path tree, versus 5.97 s for a per-path `[ -e ]` loop. Both were measured; the faster one is used and it names the missing paths rather than counting them.

hazard_2_line_endings_CORRECTED_AGAINST_.what_revision_1_of_this_file_claimed: "Git for Windows sets core.autocrlf=true in a fresh clone's local config, so a fresh Windows clone's .tf files are CRLF while the tree the committed artefacts were generated from is LF", with `infra_envs_demo_main_tf_crlf_count: {fresh_clone_default: 652, workstation_tree: 0}`.

what_this_run_measured.the one file: infra/modules/demo-api/outputs.tf — `i/crlf w/crlf`, which is the repository's own committed content faithfully checked out, not a conversion

hazard_2_line_endings_CORRECTED_AGAINST_.the_measurement_error_that_most_likely_p: `grep -c $'\r' <file>` under MSYS returns the file's LINE COUNT, not its CR count — it returned 652 for a file with zero CR bytes, on both trees. 652 is exactly `infra/envs/demo/main.tf`'s line count. This is offered as the likely cause and is labelled as a hypothesis, because the earlier session cannot be re-run. The correct measurements are `tr -dc '\r' | wc -c` and `git ls-files --eol`, and both are recorded above.
hazard_2_line_endings_CORRECTED_AGAINST_.what_stage_0_reports_now: `worktree eol   0 of 50 file(s) under infra/ converted on checkout   [byte-comparable with evidence/]`, computed from `git ls-files --eol` as `i/lf && w/crlf`, which is the only form of the difference that makes a regenerated artefact differ from a committed one. It is REPORTED, never refused: it changes no resource count.
hazard_2_line_endings_CORRECTED_AGAINST_.the_remedy_is_still_worth_giving: `git clone --config core.autocrlf=false …` writes the setting into the new repository's local config before checkout, which is the durable form; `git -c core.autocrlf=false clone …` also produced an LF tree in this run but leaves the local config unset, so a later `git checkout` in that clone can behave differently. The runbook gives the `--config` form.
hazard_2_line_endings_CORRECTED_AGAINST_.what_did_NOT_change: Revision 1's recommendation that this repository ship a `.gitattributes` pinning `*.tf text eol=lf` still stands and is still not a W4 path.

no_apply_no_credential.second_self_reported_slip_and_it_is_the_:
Two edits to `scripts/deploy/plan_repro.sh` and to this file were applied with Python's `pathlib.write_text`, which on Windows translates every `
` to `
`. Both files became CRLF, and `git diff --numstat` on the script went from a pure addition to `847 added / 612 removed` — a whole-file rewrite that would have been committed as though every line had changed. Caught by `git ls-files --eol` reporting `i/lf w/crlf`, which is the same instrument stage 0 uses. Both files were converted back with `read_bytes().replace(b'
', b'
')` and `write_bytes`, the script's diff returned to `235 added / 0 removed`, and THE WHOLE PROOF RUN WAS REPEATED against the LF bytes so that the file whose digest is recorded above is the file that was walked. Recorded because it is the line-ending hazard this evidence file documents, met from a direction the document did not name — not git, but the editor.

still_not_proven_by_this_run: Nothing was applied. Every figure here describes a plan, not a deployment.

The plan was reproduced against a LOCAL backend whose state is empty. plan_repro.sh MEASURES on every run that the remote state is empty and exits 5 when it is not, and it measured it as empty here — but the equivalence expires at the first apply and this run proves nothing about the world after one.

The console was built, the package was built, and the bundle was NOT re-captured — `capture_demo_bundle.py` needs a Cloud DSN and is a deploy step. The tracked demo-cloud fixture is what the package carries here, and the runbook says so.
`pnpm install` took 8 s against a warm pnpm store. A machine that has never installed these packages has not been measured.

The overlay is stated rather than hidden: five of the six files under test were copied into the clone because they are not yet pushed. A clone taken AFTER this wave commits will carry them, and that run has not happened.

Stage 0 refuses a checkout that is missing tracked paths. It does not detect a checkout whose files are all present and whose CONTENT has been altered — `git status --porcelain` is G0's job and this stage does not duplicate it.
